fixes.detail: The ground stays a plateau at about -1.0, and the pools (-2.05 to -3.95) and decks are cut into it as pits and trenches. That is why the water is invisible at eye level and the strip is a canyon. The terrain must step DOWN with the pools: each pool's rim and its deck share one level, and each step is open to the south and the sea, so from the overlook at -1.0 you look down over all four pools in sequence (01). This is the single blocker for the space.

66 boulders ring the pools at z -1.2 (plateau level) and 6 fail contact (dressing1:?, 2:1, 2:2, 3:3 etc. at mixed z). Snap each boulder to its own pool's rim_z, use spacing [1.5,4.0] with gaps at every spill lip, and keep the camera-side rims low so the water reads. Today they form a parapet that hides the pools.

The falls are placed at z -1.0 with h 1.6 (spanning -1.0 to 0.6), but the water spec drops from -0.65 to -2.05, so the sheet sits above the pool it feeds. Place it from z -2.05 up to -0.65 or higher, make it 4-5 m wide with an emissive or uplit white face (falls_uplight is a non-emitting 'marker'), and add a steam volume. At 23-40 m it is currently invisible.

The lantern post at (49.3,19.8) resolved at z -3.9 (deck_p4 below the overlook edge), while its pair lights3:0 is at -1.5. Snap it to the overlook at z -1.0 (dz +2.9). lights3:0 at -1.5 is also 0.5 m below the -1.0 overlook; check it.

All 'marker' lights; none emits anything visible. The pools need underwater teal emission (P1 brightest) so the water is the light source of the space, as in 01. Then thin lights[0] toro to one per pool lip (it is 8 now, two of them in the entry foreground).
